newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end up, turn around early losses.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end up, turn around early losses.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Wednesday, turning around earlier losses as the still strong underlying mood continued to underpin the market.
"The market continues to have a very firm tone," said a trader at a local bank.
Prices corrected slightly late Tuesday and Wednesday morning after sharp gains last week. Although the market rose again late this session, activity was slim, traders said.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/8 at 94, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.55 at 118.
"The market recuperated in the afternoon, but it was pretty quiet," said another trader.
With little in the way of market-moving news this session, players were awaiting the release of U.S. economic indicators in coming days for direction.
U.S. retail sales figures are due Thursday and producer prices Friday.
Traders said the market was also looking to Ecuador, where President Fabian Alarcon was expected to announce new economic measures later Wednesday.
Call money rates were flat at 5.53 percent.
